title: In China Everyone Eats Off One Plate — Genius, or a Germ Nightmare? | China Travel Expert
description:
At a Chinese meal the dishes don't come to you — they go in the middle of the table and everyone helps themselves. To make that easy, a rotating tray (the "lazy Susan") spins every dish within reach. Here's the twist most people miss: that revolving table was designed around 1915 for HYGIENE, not comfort. Dr. Wu Lien-teh, a plague-fighting physician, proposed a "hygienic dining table" with separate serving chopsticks to slow the spread of disease at communal meals. Since COVID-19, Chinese cities have pushed the same idea again — gōngkuài, a spare pair of "public chopsticks" just for taking food. So when you sit down: reach for the serving chopsticks, or just dig in with your own?

★ Expert Tip: At a round table, spin the lazy Susan clockwise and let the eldest or the guest of honour take the first bite — then it's fair game.

在中国吃饭，菜不是分到你面前，而是摆在桌子中间，大家一起夹。为了方便，一张会转的圆盘（「懒人转盘」）把每道菜转到你手边。很多人不知道的是：这种转桌大约 1915 年发明，最初是为了卫生，不是为了方便。防疫医生伍连德提出「卫生餐台」，配上公用的夹菜筷，减少聚餐时疾病传播。疫情之后，很多城市又在推同样的做法——公筷，一双专门夹菜的筷子。那么你坐下时：用公筷，还是直接用自己的筷子夹？
—
I'm mapping ALL of China — real streets, real history, zero tourist traps.
🧭 Your China Travel Expert | 你的中国旅游专家

Facts verified 2026-11-27:
• In China meals are usually shared family-style — several dishes go in the centre and everyone picks from them, and a rotating "lazy Susan" tray lets every diner reach them — Smithsonian Magazine https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/lazy-susan-classic-centerpiece-chinese-restaurants-neither-classic-nor-chinese-180949844/ + Chowhound https://chowhound.com/1643691/why-chinese-restaurants-have-round-tables
• The revolving Chinese dining table was promoted around 1915 for hygiene: Dr. Wu Lien-teh proposed a "hygienic dining table" with separate serving chopsticks to reduce disease spread at communal meals — Smithsonian Magazine https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/lazy-susan-classic-centerpiece-chinese-restaurants-neither-classic-nor-chinese-180949844/ + The News Lens https://www.thenewslens.com/article/19538
• Since 2020, Chinese cities have pushed "serving / public chopsticks" (gōngkuài) — usually longer or a different colour — to take food from shared dishes, though experts call the habit a tough sell — Sixth Tone https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1005328 + The World (PRX) https://theworld.org/stories/2020/05/25/china-sends-new-message-about-its-centuries-old-chopstick-tradition

es.title: En China todos comen del mismo plato — ¿Genial, o una pesadilla de gérmenes?
es.description: En China los platos van al centro de la mesa y todos sirven. Un tray giratorio (la "lazy Susan") acerca cada plato. El giro: esa mesa giratoria se ideó hacia 1915 por HIGIENE, no por comodidad; el Dr. Wu Lien-teh propuso una "mesa higiénica" con palillos para servir. ¿Usas los palillos comunes (gōngkuài), o los tuyos?

pt.title: Na China todos comem do mesmo prato — Genial, ou um pesadelo de germes?
pt.description: Na China os pratos vão para o centro da mesa e todos se servem. Uma bandeja giratória (a "lazy Susan") aproxima cada prato. A reviravolta: essa mesa giratória surgiu por volta de 1915 por HIGIENE, não conforto; o Dr. Wu Lien-teh propôs uma "mesa higiênica" com hashis de servir. Você usa os hashis comuns (gōngkuài), ou os seus?

id.title: Di China semua makan dari satu piring — Jenius, atau mimpi buruk kuman?
id.description: Di China lauk ditaruh di tengah meja dan semua mengambil sendiri. Nampan putar ("lazy Susan") mendekatkan tiap hidangan. Kejutannya: meja putar ini dibuat sekitar 1915 demi HIGIENE, bukan kenyamanan; Dr. Wu Lien-teh mengusulkan "meja higienis" dengan sumpit pelayan. Pakai sumpit bersama (gōngkuài), atau sumpitmu sendiri?

hi.title: चीन में सब एक ही थाली से खाते हैं — कमाल, या कीटाणुओं का खतरा?
hi.description: चीन में व्यंजन मेज़ के बीच रखे जाते हैं और सब खुद लेते हैं। एक घूमने वाली ट्रे ("लेज़ी सूज़न") हर पकवान पास ले आती है। ट्विस्ट: यह घूमती मेज़ करीब 1915 में सुविधा नहीं, सफ़ाई के लिए बनी; डॉ. वू लिएन-तेह ने परोसने के अलग चॉपस्टिक वाली "स्वच्छ मेज़" सुझाई। साझा चॉपस्टिक (gōngkuài) लें, या अपनी?

ar.title: في الصين الجميع يأكل من طبق واحد — عبقري، أم كابوس جراثيم؟
ar.description: في الصين توضع الأطباق في وسط المائدة ويخدم الجميع أنفسهم. صينية دوّارة ("lazy Susan") تقرّب كل طبق. المفاجأة: صُممت هذه المائدة الدوّارة نحو 1915 من أجل النظافة لا الراحة؛ اقترح د. وو ليان-تيه "مائدة صحية" بعيدان تقديم منفصلة. أتستخدم عيدان التقديم المشتركة (gōngkuài)، أم عيدانك؟

fr.title: En Chine, tout le monde mange dans le même plat — Génie, ou cauchemar de microbes ?
fr.description: En Chine, les plats vont au centre de la table et chacun se sert. Un plateau tournant (la "lazy Susan") rapproche chaque plat. La révélation : cette table tournante a été pensée vers 1915 par HYGIÈNE, pas par confort ; le Dr Wu Lien-teh a proposé une "table hygiénique" avec des baguettes de service. Les baguettes communes (gōngkuài), ou les vôtres ?
